title: Don't Match the Noise: Distribution Matching under Unknown Measurement Error with an Audit Sample
claim: Naive estimators are biased and audit-only ones are high-variance; combining both sources removes bias, cuts variance, and recovers the true optimum.
layout: 3 panels in a row, line plots, shared legends inside each panel
description: Three side-by-side line plots. Left: normalized error (y) against audit sample size m (x, 20 to 140). A red audit-only curve and a blue MEC-MMD curve fall steeply and then flatten. A green shaded band marks the naive noisy estimator, and a dashed black line marks the oracle at 1. MEC-MMD sits below audit-only. Middle: variance against audit size for noise levels sigma from 0.0 to 0.5, drawn as dark-blue-to-orange lines with different dash styles. All decay with m, and a green shaded region marks the audit-only variance. Right: estimated MMD squared against candidate radius r from 0 to 4. U-shaped curves for naive (red), audit-only (orange), oracle (gray) and MEC-MMD (teal). Dotted vertical lines mark each curve's minimum next to the true radius at 2.0. The teal curve's minimum falls closest to the oracle and the true radius.
caption: Left Panel. Normalized error (MSE divided by the oracle’s) versus audit size. The naive estimator is low-variance but biased, the audit-only estimator is unbiased but high-variance, and MEC-MMD removes bias while reducing variance. Middle Panel. Effect of measurement noise on MMD estimation variance for several noise levels σ. The shaded region is the audit-only variance, independent of σ. Right Panel. MEC-MMD closely matches the oracle objective and correctly identifies the true parameter with lower bias and variance. See Supplementary Materials for details.
abstract: Real-world machine learning systems often operate on imperfect measurements: sensors are noisy, annotations are produced by non-experts, and scientific observations are often indirect. In these settings, classic distribution comparison tools such as maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) can be systematically biased, matching artifacts of the measurement process rather than the underlying mechanisms of interest. We study a practical regime in which noisy observations are abundant, but only a small audited subset contains ground-truth measurements. We propose measurement-error-corrected MMD (MEC-MMD), an audit-based estimator that debiases kernel evaluations without requiring a noise model. MEC-MMD is exactly unbiased for the oracle MMD under simple random auditing, admits an explicit variance decomposition, and is consistent for the population MMD, achieving the standard $O_p(N^{-1/2})$ rate when the audit size scales with the dataset. We demonstrate the utility of distributional matching with MEC-MMD loss for both parameter estimation and unsupervised applications, showing that MEC-MMD consistently outperforms MMD and alternative methods. These results provide a principled foundation for robust distribution comparison, simulation-based inference, and learning in noisy real-world machine learning pipelines.
